# Heat Treatment Apparatus with Compact Configuration

## Overview

The present heat treatment apparatus has been developed to achieve a significantly more compact configuration compared to conventional heat treatment designs, addressing longstanding space efficiency limitations in workpiece cooling systems. This improved design accomplishes space savings while maintaining, or even enhancing, the functional performance required for effective heat treatment operations.

## Coolant Passage Defining Body

At the core of this apparatus is a coolant passage defining body, which serves the critical function of creating a dedicated coolant passage through which cooling medium is supplied directly to the workpiece undergoing heat treatment. This passage defining body ensures that coolant is delivered efficiently and consistently, enabling precise thermal management of the workpiece during the treatment process.

## Structural Composition

The coolant passage defining body is constructed from multiple discrete members, specifically comprising an upper member and a lower member. These two components are engineered to work in conjunction with one another, collectively forming the complete coolant passage when properly positioned. This dual-member construction represents a key design element that contributes to both the compactness and functional versatility of the overall apparatus.

## Operational Movement and Positioning

### Closing Configuration

The upper member and lower member are designed to be displaceable toward one another along the up-down (vertical) direction. When the members move into this closed configuration, they effectively enclose and house the workpiece securely within the coolant passage. This arrangement ensures that the workpiece is fully surrounded by the coolant passage structure, allowing for comprehensive and controlled coolant delivery during the heat treatment process.

### Opening Configuration

Conversely, the upper and lower members can also be separated from one another along the same up-down direction. This separation creates the necessary clearance to allow the workpiece to be inserted into the coolant passage or removed from it. Critically, this insertion and removal process occurs along the conveyance direction, meaning the workpiece can be transported into or out of the passage using standard conveyance methods once the members have been appropriately separated.

## Design Advantages

This dual-directional movement mechanism—wherein the upper and lower members can alternately close together and separate apart along the vertical axis—provides several key advantages:

1. **Space Efficiency**: By utilizing vertical displacement rather than more complex multi-axis movements, the apparatus achieves a more compact overall footprint.

2. **Operational Flexibility**: The ability to separate the members facilitates straightforward workpiece loading and unloading via the conveyance direction, streamlining the production workflow.

3. **Secure Enclosure**: When closed, the two-member design ensures the workpiece is properly contained within the coolant passage, promoting effective and uniform coolant application.

4. **Simplified Mechanism**: The straightforward up-down displacement design reduces mechanical complexity compared to conventional systems that may require more intricate opening and closing mechanisms.

This configuration, through its strategic use of separable upper and lower members displaceable along the up-down direction, achieves the dual objectives of maintaining a compact apparatus footprint while ensuring practical and efficient workpiece handling throughout the heat treatment process.

# Heat Treatment Apparatus with Compact Coolant Passage Design

## Background

Conventional heat treatment apparatuses used for cooling workpieces after heating processes—such as quenching applications in metal treatment—have traditionally required substantial floor space due to the arrangement of their coolant passage systems. In many existing designs, the mechanisms for containing coolant and accommodating workpiece loading/unloading operations are positioned side by side or require extended horizontal clearances, resulting in an increased overall footprint for the equipment. As manufacturing facilities increasingly prioritize space efficiency and streamlined production line layouts, there has been a growing demand for heat treatment apparatuses that can perform effective cooling operations while occupying minimal floor space.

## Summary of the Invention

The present heat treatment apparatus addresses this need for a more compact design through an innovative configuration of its coolant passage defining body. Rather than utilizing a fixed, single-piece structure, the coolant passage defining body is composed of two separate members—an upper member and a lower member—that are configured to move relative to one another along an up-down (vertical) direction.

When these two members move toward each other, they come together to collectively form an enclosed coolant passage capable of housing the workpiece during the cooling process. This passage allows coolant to circulate around or through the workpiece as needed to achieve the desired thermal treatment characteristics, such as controlled quenching rates.

Critically, the upper and lower members are also configured to separate from one another when necessary. In this separated state, a gap or opening is created that permits the workpiece to be loaded into or unloaded from the apparatus along the conveyance direction—that is, along the same horizontal path used for transporting the workpiece into and out of the treatment station.

## Advantages of the Configuration

This vertically-actuated, two-piece design offers several significant advantages over conventional side-by-side or horizontally-separating configurations:

**Space Efficiency**: Because the members separate vertically (moving upward and downward) rather than requiring horizontal displacement or extension, the apparatus does not need additional lateral floor space to accommodate the opening and closing motion. This directly contributes to a reduced overall footprint.

**Streamlined Workflow**: Since loading and unloading occur along the conveyance direction—consistent with the natural flow of workpieces through the production line—the apparatus integrates smoothly into existing manufacturing processes without requiring workpieces to be redirected or repositioned before entering the coolant passage.

**Simplified Mechanical Design**: The up-down movement mechanism for the upper and lower members can often be implemented using relatively straightforward actuation systems (such as vertical cylinders, lead screws, or similar linear actuators), potentially reducing mechanical complexity compared to systems requiring horizontal sliding or rotational opening mechanisms.

**Enhanced Sealing Potential**: When the upper and lower members move toward each other and close, the vertical mating surfaces can be designed with appropriate sealing features to ensure the coolant passage is adequately enclosed, minimizing coolant leakage during the treatment cycle.

**Flexible Integration**: This compact configuration makes the apparatus particularly well-suited for integration into production lines where floor space is at a premium, such as in facilities with multiple parallel processing stations or constrained factory layouts.

## Conclusion

By reimagining the coolant passage defining body as a two-part, vertically-actuated assembly rather than a fixed or horizontally-expanding structure, this heat treatment apparatus achieves a meaningful reduction in spatial requirements while maintaining full functionality for workpiece cooling. The alignment of the loading/unloading direction with the standard conveyance path further enhances the practical usability of this design, making it an attractive solution for manufacturers seeking to optimize both thermal processing performance and facility space utilization.

# Patent Abstract

**Heat Treatment Apparatus with Compact Coolant Passage Configuration**

A heat treatment apparatus is disclosed for cooling a workpiece following induction heating or other thermal processing, comprising an upper member and a lower member configured to cooperatively form a coolant passage surrounding the workpiece. The upper member and lower member are arranged to be movable relative to one another between an open position, permitting insertion and removal of the workpiece, and a closed position, in which the members mate to define an enclosed annular or contoured coolant passage conforming to the workpiece's outer profile.

The coolant passage is formed directly at the interface between the upper and lower members, eliminating the need for separate housing structures, external piping loops, or additional casing components that would otherwise increase the overall size of the apparatus. At least one of the upper member or lower member includes an inlet port for introducing coolant into the passage and an outlet port for discharging coolant therefrom, with the coolant flow directed circumferentially or along a predetermined path around the workpiece to achieve uniform quenching or cooling.

By integrating the coolant passage into the mating surfaces of the upper and lower members themselves, rather than relying on auxiliary jacket structures, the apparatus achieves a significantly reduced footprint and height compared to conventional quenching devices. This compact configuration allows the heat treatment apparatus to be readily incorporated into existing production lines with limited spatial clearance, while maintaining efficient and uniform cooling performance around the workpiece. The simplified two-member structure further facilitates ease of maintenance, rapid workpiece changeover, and reduced manufacturing cost relative to multi-component cooling jacket assemblies.

# Coolant Passage Defining Body with Movable Upper and Lower Members

## Overview

This technical summary describes a coolant passage defining body structure incorporating movable upper and lower members configured to facilitate workpiece loading and unloading operations along a defined conveyance direction. The mechanism enables selective opening and closing of the coolant passage to accommodate workpiece transfer while maintaining coolant containment during processing operations.

## Structural Configuration

### Primary Components

**Coolant Passage Defining Body**
The body forms an enclosed or semi-enclosed channel through which coolant fluid circulates during machining or processing operations. This structure serves the dual function of coolant containment and providing a controlled environment for the workpiece during processing.

**Upper Member**
The upper member constitutes the top portion of the coolant passage defining body and is configured for vertical or pivotal displacement relative to the lower member. This movable component:
- Forms the upper boundary of the coolant passage when in the closed position
- Retracts or displaces to create clearance for workpiece transfer
- May incorporate sealing features along its mating edges to prevent coolant leakage when closed

**Lower Member**
The lower member forms the base and lower boundary of the coolant passage, typically supporting the workpiece during processing. This component:
- Provides structural support for the workpiece transport mechanism
- May include guide rails or tracks aligned with the conveyance direction
- Works in coordination with the upper member to define the complete passage cross-section

### Movement Mechanism

The upper and lower members are configured with relative movement capability, which may be implemented through several actuation schemes:

1. **Vertical Separation**: The upper member lifts away from the lower member, creating a gap sufficient for workpiece clearance
2. **Pivoting Action**: One or both members rotate about a hinge axis to open the passage
3. **Sliding Displacement**: Members translate laterally (perpendicular to the conveyance direction) to create an opening

The movement is typically synchronized with the workpiece loading/unloading cycle, controlled via:
- Pneumatic or hydraulic cylinders
- Mechanical linkages (cam-driven or rack-and-pinion systems)
- Motor-driven actuators with position feedback

## Functional Operation

### Closed State (Processing Position)
When closed, the upper and lower members interface to form a substantially continuous coolant passage. In this configuration:
- Coolant fluid is contained and directed along the passage
- The workpiece is enclosed within the processing environment
- Sealing interfaces between members minimize fluid leakage

### Open State (Load/Unload Position)
When the members separate:
- The passage opens to permit workpiece insertion or removal along the conveyance direction
- Coolant flow may be interrupted or diverted during this phase
- The opening dimension is sized to accommodate the workpiece profile with adequate clearance

### Conveyance Direction Alignment
The opening and closing motion is coordinated with the conveyance direction such that:
- Workpieces enter and exit along a consistent linear or curvilinear path
- The upper member's opening motion does not obstruct the conveyance path
- Load and unload operations may occur at the same or opposite ends of the passage, depending on system configuration (in-line vs. return-path arrangements)

## Design Considerations

**Sealing Integrity**: The interface between upper and lower members in the closed position requires attention to sealing design (gaskets, labyrinth seals, or close-tolerance mating surfaces) to minimize coolant loss during processing.

**Cycle Time Optimization**: The opening/closing mechanism should minimize actuation time to reduce impact on overall throughput, particularly in automated production lines.

**Alignment and Repeatability**: Guide pins, tapered mating surfaces, or linear bearings may be incorporated to ensure consistent realignment of the upper member upon closing, maintaining passage geometry integrity across repeated cycles.

**Workpiece Compatibility**: The clearance dimensions in the open state must accommodate the range of workpiece sizes anticipated in the application, potentially requiring adjustable stroke length in the actuation system.

## Application Context

This type of coolant passage defining body configuration is typically employed in automated machining centers, grinding operations, or similar processes where continuous coolant application is required during processing, but periodic access for workpiece exchange is necessary. The movable member design allows integration into automated production lines with minimal manual intervention, supporting synchronized operation with upstream and downstream conveyance equipment.

# HEAT TREATMENT APPARATUS WITH VERTICALLY MOVABLE COOLANT PASSAGE MEMBERS

## FIELD OF THE INVENTION

The present invention relates generally to heat treatment apparatus for workpieces, and more particularly to a cooling device having a pair of coolant passage members configured to move vertically toward and away from one another so as to selectively enclose and release a workpiece during a cooling operation.

## BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION

In conventional heat treatment processes, workpieces subjected to elevated temperatures during hardening, tempering, or other thermal processing operations require controlled cooling to achieve desired metallurgical properties. Existing cooling apparatus often suffer from non-uniform coolant distribution, difficulty in accommodating workpieces of varying dimensions, and mechanical complexity in loading and unloading operations. There exists a need for an improved cooling apparatus that provides uniform, efficient heat extraction while facilitating straightforward workpiece handling.

## SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION

According to an aspect of the present invention, there is provided a heat treatment apparatus comprising a first coolant passage member and a second coolant passage member disposed in vertically opposed relation to one another, each of the first and second coolant passage members being movable in a vertical direction toward and away from each other between an open position, in which a workpiece may be received or removed, and a closed position, in which the first and second coolant passage members cooperatively enclose at least a portion of the workpiece to define a cooling chamber therebetween.

In an embodiment, the first coolant passage member is disposed above the workpiece support position and is configured to move downwardly toward the workpiece, while the second coolant passage member is disposed below the workpiece support position and is configured to move upwardly toward the workpiece, such that the first and second coolant passage members converge toward one another to enclose the workpiece.

Each of the first and second coolant passage members preferably comprises an internal coolant flow path, at least one coolant inlet, and a plurality of coolant discharge ports, apertures, or nozzles arranged to direct a flow of coolant medium toward an outer surface of the workpiece when the coolant passage members are in the closed position.

The apparatus may further comprise a drive mechanism operatively coupled to at least one of the first and second coolant passage members, the drive mechanism being configured to effect the vertical movement thereof. The drive mechanism may include, without limitation, a hydraulic cylinder, a pneumatic cylinder, a servo-driven ball screw assembly, a rack-and-pinion mechanism, or any combination thereof.

## DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF THE INVENTION

### General Configuration

Referring to the accompanying description of an exemplary embodiment, the heat treatment apparatus includes a frame or housing structure defining a workpiece station at which a workpiece to be cooled is positioned, for example by a conveyance mechanism, a robotic manipulator, or a manual loading operation.

A first coolant passage member is mounted above the workpiece station and supported for vertical translation relative to the frame. A second coolant passage member is mounted below the workpiece station, in vertically opposed relation to the first coolant passage member, and is likewise supported for vertical translation relative to the frame.

In the open position, the first coolant passage member is retracted upwardly and the second coolant passage member is retracted downwardly, thereby defining a clearance sufficient to permit unobstructed placement of the workpiece at the workpiece station or removal thereof following completion of the cooling cycle.

Upon initiation of a cooling cycle, the drive mechanism actuates the first coolant passage member to descend and the second coolant passage member to ascend, whereupon the two members approach one another and ultimately arrive at the closed position. In the closed position, the first and second coolant passage members may abut one another, may be separated by a predetermined gap, or may interface with an intermediate sealing member, depending upon the particular configuration and the geometry of the workpiece to be treated.

### Coolant Passage Member Construction

Each coolant passage member may be fabricated as a hollow body defining an internal chamber or a plurality of internal channels through which a coolant medium, such as water, oil, polymer quenchant, or a gas such as nitrogen or air, is circulated. Each coolant passage member is provided with at least one coolant inlet port in fluid communication with a coolant supply source, and at least one coolant outlet port in fluid communication with a coolant return or drain arrangement.

The interior-facing surface of each coolant passage member, that is, the surface confronting the workpiece when the apparatus is in the closed position, is provided with a plurality of discharge ports, orifices, nozzles, or slots configured to direct jets or streams of coolant medium onto the surface of the workpiece. The discharge ports may be arranged in a pattern selected to correspond to the geometry of the workpiece, so as to provide substantially uniform coolant coverage and, consequently, substantially uniform cooling rates across the treated surface.

In certain embodiments, the first and second coolant passage members may be contoured, recessed, or otherwise shaped so as to conform generally to an outer profile of the workpiece, thereby reducing the volume of the cooling chamber and promoting efficient coolant contact with the workpiece surface.

### Drive and Control

The vertical movement of the first and second coolant passage members may be effected independently or in coordinated fashion by the drive mechanism, which is preferably in communication with a control unit. The control unit may be configured to regulate the position, velocity, and dwell time of the coolant passage members, as well as to regulate coolant flow rate, pressure, temperature, and duration, in accordance with a predetermined heat treatment recipe corresponding to the material composition, geometry, and desired metallurgical properties of the workpiece.

In an embodiment, one or more sensors, such as position sensors, proximity switches, or linear encoders, are provided to detect the position of the first and/or second coolant passage member and to provide feedback signals to the control unit, thereby enabling precise control over the timing of the closed and open positions.

### Operation

In use, a workpiece heated to an elevated temperature, for example following an austenitizing or other thermal treatment step, is positioned at the workpiece station while the first and second coolant passage members are in the open position. The control unit thereafter actuates the drive mechanism to move the first coolant passage member downwardly and the second coolant passage member upwardly, such that the two members converge upon and enclose the workpiece, arriving at the closed position and defining the cooling chamber therebetween.

Coolant medium is thereupon supplied to the first and second coolant passage members and discharged through the respective discharge ports so as to impinge upon the surface of the enclosed workpiece, thereby extracting heat therefrom at a controlled rate for a predetermined duration.

Upon completion of the cooling cycle, the supply of coolant medium is discontinued, and the control unit actuates the drive mechanism to retract the first coolant passage member upwardly and the second coolant passage member downwardly, returning the apparatus to the open position and permitting removal of the cooled workpiece from the workpiece station.

## ADVANTAGES OF THE INVENTION

The heat treatment apparatus of the present invention provides several advantages over conventional cooling arrangements, including but not limited to: (i) enhanced uniformity of coolant application about the workpiece by virtue of the enclosing, vertically converging coolant passage members; (ii) simplified loading and unloading of workpieces owing to the retractable, vertically separable configuration of the coolant passage members; (iii) adaptability to workpieces of varying size and geometry through adjustment of the closed-position spacing and/or interchangeable coolant passage member inserts; and (iv) improved process control through coordinated regulation of coolant passage member position and coolant flow parameters.

## CLAIMS (EXEMPLARY)

**1.** A heat treatment apparatus comprising:
a first coolant passage member disposed above a workpiece station and movable in a vertical direction;
a second coolant passage member disposed below the workpiece station in vertically opposed relation to the first coolant passage member and movable in a vertical direction;
wherein the first and second coolant passage members are configured to move toward one another from an open position to a closed position so as to cooperatively enclose at least a portion of a workpiece positioned at the workpiece station, and to move away from one another from the closed position to the open position so as to release the workpiece; and
wherein each of the first and second coolant passage members defines an internal coolant flow path and a plurality of discharge ports configured to direct coolant medium toward the workpiece when the first and second coolant passage members are in the closed position.

**2.** The apparatus of claim 1, further comprising a drive mechanism operatively coupled to at least one of the first and second coolant passage members and configured to effect the vertical movement thereof.

**3.** The apparatus of claim 2, wherein the drive mechanism comprises at least one of a hydraulic cylinder, a pneumatic cylinder, a servo-driven ball screw assembly, and a rack-and-pinion mechanism.

**4.** The apparatus of claim 1, further comprising a control unit configured to regulate the vertical movement of the first and second coolant passage members and to regulate a flow of coolant medium supplied thereto.

**5.** The apparatus of claim 1, wherein the plurality of discharge ports comprises nozzles arranged in a pattern corresponding to a geometry of the workpiece.

**6.** The apparatus of claim 1, wherein at least one of the first and second coolant passage members includes a surface contoured to conform generally to an outer profile of the workpiece.

**7.** The apparatus of claim 1, further comprising at least one position sensor configured to detect a position of at least one of the first and second coolant passage members and to provide a feedback signal to a control unit.

---

You should customize the technical details (specific mechanisms, materials, dimensions, coolant types), add drawings/figures with reference numerals, and have it reviewed by a registered patent attorney or agent before filing, as claim scope and language require professional legal drafting for enforceability.*

# INVENTION DISCLOSURE

## Title of Invention
**HEAT TREATMENT APPARATUS WITH SEPARABLE COOLANT PASSAGE FOR WORKPIECE HANDLING**

---

## Field of the Invention

The present invention relates generally to heat treatment apparatus used in industrial manufacturing processes, and more particularly to a heat treatment apparatus **1** having a coolant passage system that is selectively formed and separated to facilitate insertion, positioning, and removal of a workpiece during quenching or rapid cooling operations.

---

## Background of the Invention

Conventional heat treatment apparatus typically employ fixed or rigid coolant circulation systems that surround a workpiece during the cooling phase of a heat treatment cycle. Such fixed systems often impede workpiece loading and unloading, requiring the apparatus to be disassembled or the coolant flow interrupted entirely, resulting in inefficient cycle times and inconsistent cooling rates. There exists a need for an apparatus wherein the coolant passage can be reliably formed around the workpiece during treatment and subsequently separated to allow unobstructed access for workpiece handling, without compromising the integrity or efficiency of the cooling process.

---

## Summary of the Invention

The present invention provides a heat treatment apparatus **1** comprising a first passage-forming member **40** and a second passage-forming member **42**, which are movable relative to one another between a closed position, in which the members **40**, **42** cooperate to define a continuous coolant passage **48** surrounding a workpiece **50**, and an open position, in which the members **40**, **42** are separated to permit insertion and removal of the workpiece **50**.

The coolant passage **48** is configured to direct a flow of coolant medium (e.g., quenching liquid, gas, or mist) into contact with the surface of the workpiece **50** in the closed position. A drive mechanism **100** is operably coupled to at least one of the passage-forming members **40**, **42** to effect the relative movement between the open and closed positions, thereby enabling automated or semi-automated workpiece handling in coordination with the heat treatment cycle.

---

## Detailed Description of the Invention

### 1. General Configuration

Referring to the apparatus **1**, the heat treatment apparatus comprises a housing or frame (not separately numbered) that supports a heating zone and a cooling zone. Within the cooling zone, the first passage-forming member **40** and the second passage-forming member **42** are disposed in opposing relation to one another, each having a contoured inner surface shaped to conform, at least in part, to the outer profile of the workpiece **50**.

### 2. Formation of the Coolant Passage

When the first member **40** and the second member **42** are brought together into a mating, closed configuration, their respective contoured inner surfaces cooperate to define the coolant passage **48**. The coolant passage **48** forms an enclosed or semi-enclosed channel that circumscribes the workpiece **50**, such that coolant introduced into the passage **48** flows along and around the surface of the workpiece **50** in a controlled and directed manner. This arrangement ensures uniform contact between the coolant and the workpiece **50**, promoting consistent and repeatable cooling rates, which is critical to achieving the desired metallurgical properties in the treated workpiece **50**.

The coolant passage **48** may include one or more inlet ports and outlet ports (not separately numbered) formed in the first member **40** and/or second member **42**, through which coolant is supplied and evacuated during the cooling cycle. The specific geometry of the passage **48**, including its cross-sectional area and flow path, may be tailored according to the shape and thermal mass of the workpiece **50** to optimize heat extraction.

### 3. Separation of the Passage-Forming Members

Upon completion of the cooling cycle, the first member **40** and the second member **42** are displaced relative to one another, moving from the closed position to an open position. This separation disrupts and effectively eliminates the continuous coolant passage **48**, thereby exposing the workpiece **50** and providing clearance for a handling mechanism (such as a robotic arm, conveyor, or manual operator) to access and remove the workpiece **50** from the cooling zone.

The relative movement between the first member **40** and second member **42** may be achieved through a variety of mechanical arrangements, including but not limited to:

- **Linear translation**, wherein the second member **42** slides away from the first member **40** along a guide rail or track;
- **Pivotal rotation**, wherein the second member **42** rotates about a hinge axis relative to the first member **40**;
- **Combined translational and rotational movement**, providing clearance while minimizing the overall footprint of the apparatus **1**.

### 4. Drive Mechanism

The drive mechanism **100** is operatively connected to at least the second member **42** (and optionally to the first member **40** as well, for symmetric actuation) and is configured to selectively actuate the members **40**, **42** between the closed and open positions. The drive mechanism **100** may comprise a hydraulic cylinder, pneumatic actuator, electric linear actuator, servo motor with associated gearing, or cam-driven mechanism. The drive mechanism **100** is preferably controlled by a control unit (not separately numbered) programmed to coordinate the timing of the opening and closing operations with the overall heat treatment cycle, including heating duration, cooling duration, and workpiece handling operations.

### 5. Workpiece Handling Sequence

In an exemplary operational sequence:

1. The workpiece **50** is positioned within the cooling zone while the first member **40** and second member **42** are in the open position.
2. The drive mechanism **100** actuates the members **40**, **42** into the closed position, thereby forming the coolant passage **48** around the workpiece **50**.
3. Coolant is circulated through the coolant passage **48** for a predetermined duration to achieve the desired cooling profile of the workpiece **50**.
4. Upon completion of cooling, the drive mechanism **100** actuates the members **40**, **42** into the open position, separating the coolant passage **48** and exposing the workpiece **50**.
5. The workpiece **50** is removed from the cooling zone by a handling mechanism, and a subsequent workpiece **50** may be introduced to repeat the cycle.

### 6. Advantages

The apparatus **1** as disclosed provides several advantages over conventional heat treatment systems, including:

- Improved cycle efficiency due to the elimination of manual disassembly for workpiece access;
- Enhanced cooling uniformity resulting from the precisely formed coolant passage **48**;
- Compatibility with automated workpiece handling systems, such as robotic loaders;
- Reduced thermal and mechanical stress on the apparatus **1** due to controlled, repeatable actuation of the passage-forming members **40**, **42**;
- Flexibility to accommodate workpieces **50** of varying geometries through interchangeable or adjustable passage-forming members **40**, **42**.

---

## Alternative Embodiments

In an alternative embodiment, the apparatus **1** may include more than two passage-forming members (e.g., a third member) arranged circumferentially about the workpiece **50**, such that the coolant passage **48** is defined collectively by three or more segments, each independently actuable to further optimize workpiece access from multiple directions.

# HEAT TREATMENT APPARATUS WITH VERTICALLY ACTUATED COOLANT PASSAGE MEMBERS

## FIELD OF THE INVENTION

The present invention relates to a heat treatment apparatus for cooling workpieces conveyed along a processing line, and more particularly to a compact apparatus employing a coolant passage defining body composed of separable upper and lower members configured to enclose workpieces during cooling and to release them for continued conveyance.

## BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION

Conventional cooling apparatuses used in heat treatment lines, such as those employed subsequent to quenching or annealing processes, typically require large fixed chambers through which coolant is circulated. Such chambers are frequently sized to accommodate the largest anticipated workpiece dimensions, resulting in excessive apparatus footprint and inefficient coolant consumption when treating smaller workpieces. Additionally, many conventional designs require the workpiece to be halted for extended dwell periods within the cooling chamber, thereby reducing overall line throughput. There exists a need for a heat treatment apparatus that can be reduced in overall size while maintaining effective enclosure of the workpiece during the cooling interval, and which permits rapid opening and closing of the coolant passage defining body to accommodate continuous or semi-continuous conveyance.

## SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION

According to one aspect of the present invention, there is provided a heat treatment apparatus comprising a coolant passage defining body disposed along a conveyance path of a workpiece, the coolant passage defining body comprising an upper member and a lower member that are movable relative to one another along a vertical axis between a closed position, in which the upper member and the lower member cooperate to define an enclosed coolant passage surrounding at least a portion of the workpiece, and an open position, in which the upper member and the lower member are separated to permit the workpiece to be conveyed into or out of the region between them.

The apparatus further comprises a drive mechanism operatively connected to at least one of the upper member and the lower member so as to effect vertical displacement thereof, and a coolant supply unit configured to supply a coolant fluid into the coolant passage defined between the upper member and the lower member when the coolant passage defining body is in the closed position.

By configuring the coolant passage defining body to open and close along a vertical axis in this manner, the overall apparatus can be made significantly more compact than conventional fixed-chamber designs, while still achieving efficient and uniform cooling of the workpiece. Moreover, the vertical opening and closing motion allows the apparatus to be readily integrated into an existing conveyance line without requiring extensive modification of the conveyance path itself.

## DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF THE PREFERRED EMBODIMENTS

Referring now to the drawings, wherein like reference numerals designate identical or corresponding parts throughout the several views, FIG. 1 illustrates a heat treatment apparatus 10 according to a first embodiment of the present invention.

The heat treatment apparatus 10 includes a coolant passage defining body 20 positioned along a conveyance path P extending through the apparatus. A workpiece W, such as a shaft, gear, or other machine component having undergone a preceding heating or quenching step, is conveyed along the conveyance path P by a conveyance mechanism 30, which may comprise, for example, a roller conveyor, a chain conveyor, or a plurality of transfer arms configured to advance the workpiece W in a stepwise manner.

The coolant passage defining body 20 comprises an upper member 21 and a lower member 22 disposed respectively above and below the conveyance path P. The upper member 21 has a lower surface 21a formed with a recessed portion 21b, and the lower member 22 has an upper surface 22a formed with a corresponding recessed portion 22b. When the upper member 21 and the lower member 22 are brought together, the recessed portions 21b and 22b cooperate to define an internal coolant passage 23 that substantially surrounds the outer periphery of the workpiece W, while leaving open end portions 23a and 23b through which the workpiece W may protrude or through which adjacent workpieces may be sequentially conveyed.

The upper member 21 is supported above the conveyance path P by a support frame 40 and is connected to a drive mechanism 50. In the illustrated embodiment, the drive mechanism 50 comprises a hydraulic cylinder 51 having a piston rod 52 connected to an upper surface of the upper member 21, such that actuation of the hydraulic cylinder 51 raises and lowers the upper member 21 along a vertical axis A. It should be noted that the drive mechanism 50 is not limited to a hydraulic cylinder, and may alternatively comprise a pneumatic cylinder, an electric linear actuator, a rack-and-pinion mechanism, or a cam-driven linkage, without departing from the scope of the present invention.

In the illustrated embodiment, the lower member 22 is fixedly mounted to a base 60 and remains stationary relative to the conveyance path P during operation; however, in an alternative embodiment described below with reference to FIG. 3, both the upper member 21 and the lower member 22 are configured to be independently displaceable along the vertical axis A, thereby permitting the coolant passage defining body 20 to be opened and closed with a reduced overall stroke length for each member, further contributing to the compactness of the apparatus.

A coolant supply unit 70 is fluidly connected to the coolant passage 23 by way of a supply conduit 71 communicating with an inlet port 24 formed in the lower member 22, and a discharge conduit 72 communicating with an outlet port 25 formed in the upper member 21. The coolant supply unit 70 is configured to supply a coolant fluid, such as water, oil, or a water-soluble quenching medium, into the coolant passage 23 at a predetermined flow rate and pressure once the coolant passage defining body 20 has reached the closed position, and to interrupt or reduce the flow of coolant fluid prior to the upper member 21 being raised to the open position.

Operation of the apparatus 10 will now be described. In an initial state, the upper member 21 is maintained in a raised, open position by the drive mechanism 50, such that a gap sufficient to permit passage of the workpiece W is defined between the lower surface 21a of the upper member 21 and the upper surface 22a of the lower member 22. The conveyance mechanism 30 advances the workpiece W along the conveyance path P until the workpiece W is positioned within the region bounded by the recessed portions 21b and 22b.

Upon detection of the workpiece W in the proper position, which may be accomplished by means of a sensor 80, such as a photoelectric sensor or a limit switch, disposed adjacent the conveyance path P, a control unit 90 actuates the drive mechanism 50 so as to lower the upper member 21 along the vertical axis A until the lower surface 21a of the upper member 21 contacts, or is brought into close proximity with, the upper surface 22a of the lower member 22, thereby placing the coolant passage defining body 20 in the closed position and enclosing the workpiece W within the coolant passage 23.

The control unit 90 then actuates the coolant supply unit 70 to supply coolant fluid into the coolant passage 23 for a predetermined duration, sufficient to achieve the desired cooling rate and final temperature of the workpiece W. During this interval, the coolant fluid flows about the outer periphery of the workpiece W within the coolant passage 23 and is discharged through the outlet port 25 and discharge conduit 72 to a coolant recovery unit, not shown, for filtration and recirculation.

Upon completion of the predetermined cooling duration, the control unit 90 interrupts the supply of coolant fluid and actuates the drive mechanism 50 to raise the upper member 21 along the vertical axis A, thereby returning the coolant passage defining body 20 to the open position and releasing the workpiece W. The conveyance mechanism 30 then advances the workpiece W out of the apparatus 10 and along the conveyance path P to a subsequent processing station, while a succeeding workpiece W is simultaneously advanced into the region between the upper member 21 and the lower member 22 to repeat the cycle described above.

It will be appreciated that, because the upper member 21 and the lower member 22 move only along the vertical axis A to open and close the coolant passage defining body 20, the horizontal footprint of the apparatus 10 may be minimized relative to conventional cooling chambers requiring lateral clearance for opening mechanisms, thereby facilitating installation of the apparatus 10 within confined spaces along an existing heat treatment line.

In a further embodiment, illustrated in FIG. 3, the lower member 22 is likewise connected to a second drive mechanism 55, such that the upper member 21 and the lower member 22 move toward one another symmetrically about a fixed horizontal reference plane B corresponding to the conveyance path P. This configuration is particularly advantageous where the workpiece W is conveyed at a fixed elevation and it is desired to minimize the vertical stroke of either member individually, or where it is desired to reduce the magnitude of impact forces generated upon closure of the coolant passage defining body 20.

It is to be understood that the recessed portions 21b, 22b may be provided with a plurality of coolant discharge nozzles or apertures distributed along their respective inner surfaces, so as to direct jets of coolant fluid directly against the outer surface of the workpiece W, thereby enhancing the uniformity and rate of heat extraction. Additionally, the coolant passage defining body 20 may be provided with a sealing member, such as an elastomeric gasket or a labyrinth seal, disposed along the peripheral edges of the recessed portions 21b, 22b, so as to minimize leakage of coolant fluid when the coolant passage defining body 20 is in the closed position.

While the foregoing description has been made with reference to specific embodiments, it will be understood by those skilled in the art that various changes may be made and equivalents may be substituted without departing from the true spirit and scope of the present invention.
